scenes.text: Hello little friend! I'm Chirpy Birdie. Today, we're going on an amazing journey about emotional regulation. Are you ready? I'm so curious about what we'll discover together. It's going to be a fun adventure, full of learning and smiles.

Emotional regulation is like when we learn to manage our feelings. Sometimes we feel happy, like when we get a big hug. Other times, we might feel sad, like when a toy breaks. It's okay to have all these feelings. What's important is how we handle them. Let's find out how we can do that together.

One way to manage our feelings is by taking deep breaths. Let's try it together! Breathe in slowly through your nose like you're smelling a beautiful flower. Then, breathe out gently through your mouth like you're blowing a soft, fluffy cloud away. Doesn't that feel nice and calming?

Great job on those breaths! You did it like a pro. Breathing helps us feel calmer and more in control. Next time you feel upset or angry, remember this little trick. You can count to three while you breathe, and it will help you feel better. Let's give it another try!

Now that we know how to breathe deeply, let's talk about using our words. When we feel something, it's good to say how we feel. You can say, 'I'm feeling sad,' or 'I'm so excited!' This helps others understand us better. Can you think of a time you used your words to tell someone how you felt?

When we tell someone how we feel, it can help us feel better. If you're feeling mad because someone took your toy, you can say, 'I feel mad because I want to play with that, too.' This way, others know how to help you. It's like sharing a secret that helps everyone understand.

Wonderful! You're doing such an amazing job learning about feelings. Remember, it's okay to have big feelings. Everyone does! You're learning how to be a feelings detective, discovering what's inside. Keep it up, and you'll be a feelings expert in no time!

Sometimes, when we have big feelings, it helps to take a break. If you're feeling overwhelmed, find a quiet spot to sit or lie down. You can close your eyes and imagine a peaceful place. Maybe a sunny beach or a cozy blanket fort. Taking a break can make everything feel a bit better.

Let's practice imagining a peaceful place together. Close your eyes and think about your favorite spot. Is it a park with lots of green trees? Or perhaps a room filled with all your favorite toys? Imagine being there and feeling calm and happy. Doesn't that feel wonderful?

You're doing fantastic! Imagining peaceful places is a great way to help your mind relax. It's like giving your brain a little hug. Whenever you feel a bit wobbly, remember you can always visit your special place in your mind. You're becoming so skilled at this!

Now, let's talk about playing. Playing is a wonderful way to express our feelings. When we play, we can be anyone we want, like a superhero or a brave explorer. Through play, we can let our feelings out and even understand them better. What's your favorite game to play?

Do you remember a time when playing helped you feel better? Maybe you were feeling a bit lonely, and then you played with a friend. Or perhaps you were feeling bored, and you started a new game. Isn't it amazing how play can change how we feel? What do you think?

Let's remember all the things we've learned today. We practiced deep breathing to calm down. We learned to use our words to share how we feel. We imagined peaceful places to rest our minds. And we talked about how play helps us express our feelings. These are all tools you can use every day.

You're such a great learner! I'm so proud of you for trying all these new things. Remember, everyone has feelings, and it's okay to feel them. The important part is how we handle them. Keep practicing, and you'll keep getting stronger and happier every day!

It's time to say goodbye for now. But remember, Chirpy Birdie is always here to help you with your feelings. Keep practicing and having fun with your new skills. You can always come back and join me for more adventures. Goodbye, little friend! Until next time, keep smiling and being brave!
